Second, we initially had no means by which to automatically differentiate between the interior of an object and an open area of the measurement space which simply had not yet been measured. As an example, Fig. 10, which is from a 2017 publication [48], shows a volumetric reconstruction of a 137Cs source within a cardboard box, where we manually specified to the SDF algorithm that the volume within that box should be fully voxelized. In fact, it was in 2017 that the concept of the truncated sign distance field (TSDF) gained traction in applications to robotic sensing and planning [49]. Recent implementation of TSDF space representations and semantic segmentation algorithms within the SDF framework (described below) enable automation of logic that was previously implemented manually; the interior of objects can be automatically identified and provided to an algorithm and unseen areas are considered logically different from empty observed space. LBNL has begun to implement an algorithm that will assume un-observed spaces within visually-labeled objects such as e.g., boxes, ducts, or containers should be voxelized for consideration as potential radioactive sources, rather than just at their surfaces. Figure 10. Three views of a volumetric Compton imaging reconstruction of a 30µCi 137Cs source place within a cardboard box. The detector trajectory is shown as a white line, where the time of detection of each event that was included in the Compton image (e.g., doubles summing to near 662 keV) is shown as a red dot. The coloring of the 3D map represents 137Cs activity. Another advancement related to volumetric SDF imaging is the incorporation of attenuation into SDF analyses. In Ref. [50], it is described how a single free parameter can be used to describe attenuation in SDF analyses, and that doing so substantially improves the quality of PSL reconstructions. Once again, the voxel grid was assigned manually, rather than through some automated reduction of semantic scene information. Nonetheless, Fig. 11 shows a comparison of the PSL localization algorithm operating on a measurement of a source located within one of three partially filled cargo containers that were positioned adjacent one another. The blue ‘x’ is centered on the source location. The orange coloring in Fig. 11 indicates the 95% statistical confidence interval for the standard PSL algorithm’s fit of the source location. This algorithm’s output, which ignored attenuation, is compared to the red coloring which is the corresponding output of the PSL algorithm when a single attenuation parameter is concurrently fit. Clearly, including attenuation significantly improved the accuracy of the PSL algorithm output. It should be reiterated that the volume for volumetric imaging was selected manually, rather than through any autonomous and/or semantic data process algorithms. An NA-22 Innovation portfolio project demonstrated that thru-wall radar techniques can also provide information for attenuation corrections [51]. Integration of such capabilities with SDF would be an attractive R&D opportunity for unilateral and low-profile radiation detection activities.
